extracted.intended_audience: plant breeders, seed companies, applicants, and attorneys/agents seeking plant variety protection in the United States (USDA/Plant Variety Protection Office practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for seeking, obtaining, defending, and enforcing plant variety protection in the United States under the Plant Variety Protection Act and 7 CFR Part 97 regulations, including definitions, application content and form, examination, priority/protest procedures, appeals, remedies, and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essentially derived variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'essentially derived variety' means a variety that (i) is predominantly derived from another variety (the 'initial variety') or from a variety that is predominantly derived from the initial variety, while retaining the expression of the essential characteristics that result from the genotype or combination of genotypes of the initial variety; (ii) is clearly distinguishable from the initial variety; and (iii) except for differences that result from the act of derivation, conforms to the initial variety in the expression of the essential characteristics that result from the genotype or combination of genotypes of the initial variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods of obtaining an essentially derived variety may include selection of a natural or induced mutant or somaclonal variant, selection of a variant individual from plants of the initial variety, backcrossing, transformation by genetic engineering, or other method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeder (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'breeder' means the person who directs the final breeding creating a variety or who discovers and develops a variety. If the actions are conducted by an agent on behalf of a principal, the principal, rather than the agent, shall be considered the breeder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term does not include a person who redevelops or rediscovers a variety the existence of which is publicly known or a matter of common knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'variety' means a plant grouping within a single botanical taxon of the lowest known rank, that ... can be defined by the expression of the characteristics resulting from a given genotype or combination of genotypes, distinguished from any other plant grouping by the expression of at least one characteristic and considered as a unit with regard to the suitability of the plant grouping for being propagated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition used for determining what is the subject matter eligible for protection and for DUS (distinctness, uniformity, stability) style assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kind, seed, sexually reproduced, tuber-propagated (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kind means one or more related species or subspecies known by one common name (e.g., soybean). 'Seed' for tuber-propagated varieties means tuber or part used for propagation. 'Sexually reproduced' includes production by seed, but does not include production by tuber propagation. 'Tuber propagated' means propagated by a tuber or part of a tuber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitional criteria prescribe which plant reproduction methods fall within the Act and regulations and how to interpret claims and specimen requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary may establish regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may establish regulations, not inconsistent with law, for the conduct of proceedings in the Plant Variety Protection Office after consultations with the Plant Variety Protection Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework authority — many specific procedural and substantive requirements follow by regulation (§97.x series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Variety Protection Board composition and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Board shall consist of experts in varietal development with farmer representation and roughly equal private/seed industry and government/public sector representation. The Secretary (or designee) chairs without voting except to break ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board advises Secretary on rules and regulations, reviews appeals from examiners, may act by panels, and advises on matters under section 44 (public interest in wide usage). Members serve without compensation except reimbursable expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees — Secretary authorized to charge and collect reasonable fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary shall, under such regulations as the Secretary may prescribe, charge and collect reasonable fees for services performed under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late-payment penalties and interest may be assessed; collected funds credited to the account that incurs the cost and remain available without fiscal year limitation; Attorney General may bring actions for recovery of unpaid charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of papers and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may by regulation prescribe the form of papers to be filed in the Plant Variety Protection Office. Applications have specified parts and content (§97.5–§97.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations set detailed requirements such as specimen requirements, drawings, photographs, and the parts that must be filed together. See §§97.5–97.12 (general requirements, application for certificate, specimen requirements, drawings/photographs, parts to be filed together, filing date rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen requirements (§97.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must meet specimen requirements as prescribed by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimen standards (how to submit plant material for testing/validation) are set in the regulations; failure to meet specimen requirements can affect examination and issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and photographs (§97.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may include drawings and photographs as specified in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual material should conform to regulatory standards for format and content to support variety descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts of an application to be filed together (§97.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain parts of an application must be filed together as required by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures completeness for filing and proper assignment of filing dates; see §97.11–§97.12 for filing/date consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application accepted and filed when received; filing date rules (§97.11-12)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is accepted and filed when received if it meets criteria; rules establish number and filing date of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations govern when a submission qualifies as a filed application and the consequences for priority and benefit of earlier filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential handling of applications (§97.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are handled in confidence to the extent provided by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality provisions apply during pendency; limited publication rules set out what becomes public and when (§97.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of pending applications (§97.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide for publication of pending applications (subject to confidentiality rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication timing and content are regulated; publication of varietal descriptions does not constitute recognition of DUS (distinctness, uniformity, stability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to respond within time limit (§97.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be abandoned for failure to respond within the time limit prescribed by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations provide for extensions (§97.21), revival (§97.22), and voluntary withdrawal/abandonment (§97.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by applicant (§97.16, §97.108)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may amend their applications subject to regulatory limits, including after final action in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules govern when and how amendments are allowed (after allowance, after final action) and any binding effects if Secretary allows certificate based on amended application (§97.302).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of applications (§97.100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are examined by the Office under the examination rules set forth in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may issue notices, require replies, and refer matters to the Commissioner or Board as needed; see follow-on sections on notice of allowance and denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allowance and issuance (§97.101–103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide for notice of allowance and the process for issuance of a certificate once requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowances may be accompanied by requirements for amendments, fees, or specimen compliance prior to certificate issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of an application and reply/reconsideration (§97.105–107)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations set procedures for denial, applicant reply, requests for reconsideration, and initial appeals from examiner/adverse actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants have opportunities to reply and seek reconsideration and initial appeals; timelines and procedural forms are regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors in certificate — office or applicant mistake (§97.120–121)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations allow correction of certificates for Office mistakes and for applicant mistakes under prescribed procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate procedures apply depending on whether the error originated with the Office or the applicant; see §§97.120–121 for rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissuance / certified seed only election (§97.122)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations include a provision for reissuance of certificate and for a certified seed only election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holders may elect a 'certified seed only' status under regulatory conditions; reissuance procedures are governed by rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments and recording (§97.130–132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording of assignments is regulated; conditional assignments and public inspection of assignment records are provided for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned varieties and certificates have special filing/recording rules; assignment records are open for inspection under conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking or labeling provisions (§97.140–144)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations prescribe marking/labeling requirements after filing, after issuance, for testing/increase, certified seed only, and additional marking or labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper marking/labeling affects damages limitation and notice defenses in infringement actions (see section 127 in Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be represented; authorization and professional conduct (§97.150–157, §97.157–158)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons have a right to be represented; rules cover authorization, revocation, recognized persons, government employees, signatures, addresses, professional conduct, and advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary prescribes admission to practice and may suspend/exclude persons shown to be incompetent or disreputable; unauthorized practice liability exists (§26–27 of Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and refunds; payment methods (§97.175–179)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations list fees and charges, advance payment requirements, methods of payment, refunds, and costs for copies/certified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific fee amounts and procedural rules are set by regulation; late payments incur penalties under statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of office records (§97.190)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules specify when open records are available and under what conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access to records is governed by the regulations and confidentiality provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest proceedings (§97.200–201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide procedures for protests to the grant of a certificate and conduct of protest proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protest mechanisms allow third parties to raise objections; procedural timelines and evidence rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority contest definition and preparation (§97.205–209)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of a priority contest, when declared, and preparation requirements for priority proceedings and papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations set burden of proof, preliminary statements, sealed statements, and when priority contests are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary statement contents (§97.209)
rubrics_metrics.description: In filing a preliminary statement each party must show: (1) the date of first determination of the novel variety, (2) the date of the first written description (or state none existed), (3) the date of first acts susceptible of proof that would establish determination and a brief description of such acts (or state none), and (4) the date of actual production (or state none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When alleging a first written description, a copy must be attached. If relying on a prior domestic or foreign application the preliminary statement must identify it and copies (with translations for foreign filings) will be served on interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary statement for foreign-developed varieties (§97.210)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the novel variety was developed in a foreign country, the preliminary statement must show the information specified in §97.209 and whether, when, and under what circumstances the variety was introduced into the United States by or on behalf of the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign-filed prior applications relied upon must be identified and English translations provided for service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements sealed before filing (§97.211)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary statements shall be submitted in a sealed envelope bearing the filer’s name and the contest number/title and enclosed in an outer envelope marked 'To Be Opened Only by the Commissioner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures confidentiality until the time for filing has closed; duplicate copies filed with Office so that copy can be forwarded to opposing parties once both have filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of preliminary statement on motion (§97.212)
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of material error arising through inadvertence or mistake, a preliminary statement may be corrected upon a satisfactory showing to the Commissioner that the correction is of material significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction must be made as soon as practicable after discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file preliminary statements consequence (§97.213)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any party to a priority contest fails to file a preliminary statement, he or she shall be restricted to his or her earliest effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanction for failure to participate in priority proceedings — may be dispositive of priority issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to preliminary statements (§97.214)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary statements shall be open to inspection by any party after the date set for filing of preliminary statements, but shall not be open prior to that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects secrecy until both parties have filed; then statements become discoverable among the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner may dissolve/suspend priority contest if ineligibility arises (§97.215–219)
rubrics_metrics.description: If information arises during a priority contest that may render the variety ineligible for a certificate, the Commissioner may suspend the contest and refer the matter to an examiner; parties will be notified and allowed to file arguments within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may remand, continue, modify, or dismiss suspension; may direct attention to irregularities amounting to a bar to granting a certificate and refer matters to Board for advisory decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision by the Commissioner in priority contests (§97.220)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a priority contest is concluded on preliminary statements or proposed findings, the Commissioner issues proposed findings and gives parties not less than 30 days to show cause why they should not be made final; additional affidavits/exhibits not considered except on good cause. Final findings and notice of priority will then be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision entered against a party whose preliminary statement alleges a date of determination later than the other party's application filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of defeated applicant claims (§97.221)
rubrics_metrics.description: After final notice of priority and expiration of appeal time, the claims constituting the priority issue stand finally disposed of without further action by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finality rule for priority determinations — precludes further administrative re-litigation of same priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second priority contest barred (§97.222)
rubrics_metrics.description: A second priority contest between the same parties shall not be entertained by the Commissioner for the same novel variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits repetitive contests between same parties on same variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Secretary — petition content and timing (§97.300)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition to the Secretary may be made from final actions of the Commissioner denying or refusing to allow a certificate or adverse decisions under specified sections; petition must state facts, points to be reviewed, actions requested, be filed in duplicate, include prescribed fee, and generally be filed within 60 days of the action complained of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary may provide opportunity for oral presentation informally or by formal hearing; formal hearings follow other specific rules of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's answer and appellant reply (§97.301)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may furnish a written answer to the Secretary with explanation and supply a copy to the appellant. Within 20 days of such answer the appellant may file a reply addressing only new points raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short and specific reply window — limits scope of appellate briefing to new issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision by the Secretary (§97.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary, after receiving advice of the Board, may affirm or reverse the Commissioner's decision in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Secretary's decision explicitly states a certificate be allowed based on an amended application, the applicant may amend accordingly and the decision is binding on the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action following Secretary decision (§97.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Secretary’s decision shall be served on appellant and Commissioner; when appeal petition dismissed or time for court appeal expired without filing, proceedings are terminated unless further action required; Secretary's decision is stayed if appealed to court until outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural consequences of appeals and effect on administrative process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time on showing of good cause (§97.400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a showing of good cause, extensions of time not otherwise provided for may be granted by the Commissioner or, if an appeal has been filed, by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility for timing but requires demonstration of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous petitions and timeliness (§97.401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for reconsideration or modification in priority or protest proceedings shall be filed within 20 days after decision; Commissioner may consider petitions relating to abuse of discretion but untimely petitions may be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict short timelines for post-decision petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers and manner (§97.402–403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper required to be served and filed must be served by the Secretary in prescribed manners. Service on an attorney/agent if there is one, otherwise on party. Methods include certified mail (return receipt controlling date), leaving copy at usual place of business with an employee, leaving at home with a family member over 14, or, if none practicable, publication in Office Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of service of supporting papers must be made before such papers will be considered; service rules affect effective dates and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to U.S. Courts; certified record ( §97.500 )
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with Secretary's decision may appeal to appropriate federal courts or institute a civil action in U.S. District Court as set forth in the Act; appellant must notify Secretary, state reasons for appeal, and obtain a certified copy of the record which the Office forwards to the Court on order and at the appellant's expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial review procedures mirror other administrative appeals and require careful handling of the record and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cease and desist proceedings (false marking) (§97.600)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings under section 128 of the Act for false marking are conducted in accordance with rules of practice under the Federal Seed Act, with references to 'Examiner' construed to be Administrative Law Judge, USDA, rather than Examiner under PVPA regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False marking and cease-and-desist procedures follow specific cross-referenced rules; penalties and processes are governed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use declaration/public interest in wide usage (§97.700)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Secretary believes a protected variety should be declared open to public use under section 44, the owner shall be given notice and opportunity to present views orally or in writing; Secretary refers matter to the Board for advice on limitations or rate of remuneration and will announce decisions by press release when the variety is declared open to public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner input and Board advice required; decisions not to declare are transmitted only to owner and Board members (no public announcement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of public variety descriptions (§97.800)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary submissions of varietal descriptions of 'public varieties' will be accepted for publication in the Official Journal; such publication shall not constitute recognition that the variety is distinct, uniform, and stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is informational only and does not equate to issuance of protection or DUS recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony, affidavits, depositions, subpoenas (§23–24 statutory; §97.217 regs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary may establish regulations for taking affidavits, depositions, and other evidence; clerks of U.S. courts shall issue subpoenas for witnesses as provided; affidavits and exhibits including official records and printed publications may be introduced as evidence in priority contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal civil procedure rules on attendance and production apply insofar as consistent; witnesses entitled to fees/travel expenses; specific affidavit/exhibit handling and service rules in regs (copies served on other interested parties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters considered in determining priority — only priority of development (§97.218)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining priority, the Commissioner will consider only priority of development based on evidence submitted. Questions of novelty generally will not be considered in the decision on priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority contests focus on who first developed/determined the variety, not on broader protectability/novelty issues (which may be considered separately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of defective execution (§25 statute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document required to be executed in a specified manner may be provisionally accepted despite defective execution, provided a properly executed document is submitted within such time as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides administrative flexibility to cure formal execution defects within time limits set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice and sanctions (§26–27 statute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary shall prescribe regulations governing admission to practice and conduct of persons representing applicants; anyone engaging in practice while suspended, excluded, or without admission is liable for return of money received and compensation for damage and may be enjoined, subject to exceptions for supervised work or employer-employee situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may suspend/exclude persons after notice and hearing for incompetence, disreputability, or gross misconduct; unauthorized practice provisions also describe defenses to liability if work was competent and without negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies, presumption of validity, defenses, injunctions, damages, attorney fees (Act chapters)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides remedies for infringement of plant variety protection, including injunctions, damages, presumption of validity and available defenses, assessment of attorney fees, time limitations on damages, limitations tied to marking and notice, false marking sanctions, and special service rules for nonresident proprietors and state entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory and statutory interplay determines how remedies are pursued, limitations on recoverable damages (e.g., marking/notice), and enforcement against various classes of defendants (including states). (See CHAPTER 12 in Act and related regulations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement exemptions — save seed, crop, research, intermediary (Act chapters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Act includes a grandfather clause and exemptions: right to save seed/crop exemption, research exemption, intermediary exemption (see sections 112–115).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory exemptions define permitted uses that do not constitute infringement; details and limits are given in the Act and implemented in related regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination after issue and interfering certificates (CHAPTER 9 / §91–92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations provide for reexamination after issue and for handling interfering plant variety protection claims (priority/interference-like proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-issuance proceedings can challenge validity or raise interference issues; procedures and grounds are regulated.
